correctness.rationale: For every nonempty finite-abelian packing B the necessary-and-sufficient independence and domination conditions follow directly from A-A. In characteristic two D is exactly a four-element subgroup; in characteristic three it is either a three-element subgroup or the nine-element plane minus one three-element line except zero. These force all maximal packings and yield the displayed exact counts. Exhaustive checker covers every anchored three-subset and every candidate packing B in cyclic primes 5,7,11, and explicitly certifies two different maximal packings in each rank-two group of those characteristics. The rank extension is a direct product with a complementary vector space. For all primes at least 13, cyclic gaps 4..7 give independent dominating sets of two different sizes; arithmetic proves the gap feasibility for every such prime. Small-field exhaustive checks agree, but the universal argument is symbolic. No unsupported extrapolation or unproved lemma remains.

originality.rationale: The 2026 paper studies two-element cyclic supports and explicitly calls for the three-element extension. The 2023 paper proves all-subset stability and reports some small negative cases, but the presence of unstable supports of size four does not determine three-point stability. The new claim is the exact classification of all elementary abelian three-point-stable groups together with exact coset classifications/counts of every subfactor in characteristics two and three. Previously recorded \(C_5^2\) and \(C_7^2\) instability is expressly not claimed new. No equivalent published claim or stronger covering theorem was identified in the inspected primary texts, published abstract sources, prior known claims, or semantic mathematical searches; historical priority remains qualified.
residual_risks: Possible implicit derivation from older general well-covered Cayley-graph or circulant/triangular-torus classifications not identified by exact source search.

value.rationale: A natural 2026 three-support extension of group subindices admits an exact all-prime/all-rank classification for an infinite family. In characteristics two and three the theorem provides a complete structural description and explicit doubly exponential counts of every maximal packing, showing a genuine all-rank positive regime even for some groups not stable under all support sizes. Negative directions give explicit rank-independent separating witnesses. The result is not a textbook restatement, arbitrary small slice, or a recomputation of known small-group tables.
